title: HouseGraph save file (format version 4)
description: The canonical shape GraphFileIO writes for version 4, exactly as documented in docs/engine/save-format.md. HouseGraph's own reader is more forgiving than this schema: a file written before versioning existed, or before a given key existed, uses a legacy positional shape this schema does not describe (see save-format.md's 'Forgiving reads' section). Validate a graph an agent harness is about to write against this schema; do not use a failure here as proof an existing, older file won't open.

plugins.description: Present only when the graph uses a node type from an out-of-tree library.

module.description: This graph's own identity as a module, present only on a graph that has been published as one. The id is the identity a consumer stores; the name is a label. See docs/decisions/0011-modules-are-referenced-by-id.md.

modules.description: The modules this graph references, present only when it references one. Each row is named by the 'module' key of one or more nodes.

groups.description: The labelled rectangles drawn behind the graph, present only when the canvas holds one. Purely a view concern: a frame is inert at run time, and a graph loaded without them runs identically. A frame holds no list of what it contains — membership is recomputed from the rectangle, so a node belongs to every frame whose rectangle encloses it whole, and the larger of two nested frames is the one that commands the other. Nothing references a row, so rows carry no id and their order is only the order they were created in.

moduleRow.description: One module this graph references. 'path' is a resolution hint recording where the module was last found; it is never the identity, and a file at that path carrying a different id is a different module. 'plugins' names the node libraries the MODULE needs — recorded here at save time, while the module was resolvable, so the load-time dependency check stays a pure read of this one root with no file opened.

portRef.description: A data or flow port endpoint: the port's name when it is non-blank and unique on its node, otherwise its zero-based position.

valueEntry.description: One input or output slot, keyed by name. 'value' is null for a computed, secret or transient variable (see NodeVariable.isPersistentValue) or a slot that was never set.

type.description: The stable type id (NodeRegistry.persistentTypeId): a node's simple class name by default, or an explicit @Node.Type id.

plugin.description: The library id from the root 'plugins' table that provides this node type. Absent for a built-in node.

module.description: The module id from the root 'modules' table this node references. Only a ModuleNode writes it; the node keeps the same id in its own 'state', which is where the reference lives — this key is the pointer that makes the table readable before any node is built.

nodeSignature.description: A fingerprint of this node type's ports, flow ports and default state at save time (see the catalog/NodeSignature class). Compare against the same type's currently-installed signature (the 'nodes check' CLI command, or the node catalog's 'signature' field) to detect a library update that changed this node's shape since the graph was saved. Absent on a save written before this field existed.

requiredInputs.description: Names of inputs that must have a value source for the node to be considered configured.

node.description: additionalProperties stays open: a node type this build cannot resolve (MissingNode) is written back byte-for-byte, including keys a newer format added that this schema does not yet know about.

group.description: One group frame. The reader is more forgiving than this: every key is defaulted when absent, and a width or height below the minimum is clamped to something the user can still grab.

title.description: The label drawn at the frame's top-left. May be empty, which renders as a placeholder.

color.description: The frame's colour as a CSS hex string, e.g. "#61afef".
